findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request finishes
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the goroutine that writes to the legacy store derives its 10-second-timeout context from the incoming request context (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). The parent `ctx` is cancelled as soon as the HTTP request that triggered the write completes, so the legacy write is very likely aborted immediately rather than running for the intended 10 seconds. This defeats the purpose of the 'safe measure' write to legacy: legacy storage will silently miss writes whenever the client disconnects or the request handler returns quickly, leaving the two stores permanently divergent with no error surfaced. The goroutine should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or a background context) as the parent.

findings.title: DeleteCollection async legacy call records metric as 'storage' duration
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine, the legacy delete result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. This pollutes the `unified_storage_write_duration`/legacy metric series with legacy-store latencies and error counts, making the dual-writer metrics wrong and misleading for anyone monitoring migration progress.

findings.title: Storage failures recorded under the legacy metric in Create and Update
findings.body: In `Create` (line 45) and `Update` (line 129), the error path when the unified Storage call fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. This records a failed, zero-length 'legacy' operation that never happened, corrupting legacy-store error-rate and duration metrics. It should be `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` to match the Delete and DeleteCollection error paths.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name instead of kind as label
findings.body: On the Delete success path, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind` as the label. Since object names are unbounded user-controlled values, this creates unbounded label cardinality in Prometheus (one metric series per deleted object name) and inconsistent labeling versus the failure path on line 103. It should pass `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Delete puts the base logger into the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: In `Delete`, `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses the base `d.Log` rather than the locally built `log` (with name/kind/method values) that every other method uses. Any logger retrieved from the context downstream (including in the async legacy goroutine, which inherits this ctx) will be missing the name and kind fields, making log correlation for deletes inconsistent.

findings.title: Tests spawn unmocked async legacy calls that can panic or race in goroutines
findings.body: Mode 3 now performs the legacy write in a background goroutine, but the tests never wait for it and in several success cases never stub it: TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection set up no `Legacy.Delete`/`Legacy.DeleteCollection` mock expectations, and TestMode3_Create's second case stubs only the legacy mock. testify's `mock.Mock` panics on calls to methods with no expected call, so these goroutines can panic non-deterministically after the subtest finishes, causing flaky suite crashes. Additionally, since the goroutine's error is never returned or awaited, no test actually verifies that the legacy write happens, times out, or that legacy failures are correctly logged/metriced — the core behavior of this PR is untested.

findings.title: No retry, queue, or error surfacing for failed legacy writes
findings.body: All legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines: if `d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete` fails (or the derived context is cancelled per the context issue), the error is only swallowed into a metric — there is no logging of the failure, no retry, and no reconciliation mechanism. Once mode 3 is the default, any transient legacy failure leaves the legacy database permanently out of sync, which matters because legacy Grafana APIs and other code paths still read from legacy storage. At minimum the goroutines should log the legacy error, and the team should confirm a backfill/reconciliation job exists before enabling mode 3.
